facts.text: ZaberStage maps one actuator alias per device to each of the x, y and z axes; set_x_axis, set_y_axis and set_z_axis select the actuator by its alias
get_positions returns each configured axis position in microsteps multiplied by that axis's microstep size
move_x_absolute, move_y_absolute and move_z_absolute divide the requested position by the axis's microstep size before sending it to the actuator
The microstep size is set on the stage object with set_x_microstep_size, set_y_microstep_size and set_z_microstep_size; the stage does not read it from the device
The travel is set on the stage object with set_x_travel, set_y_travel and set_z_travel; the stage does not read it from the device
The README tells the operator to look up the microstep size and the travel range of the connected actuator model on the Zaber website and set them on the stage
ZaberStage.home calls home on every device in the chain
ZaberStage.stop calls stop on every device in the chain
ZaberDevice.stop sends command 23, which stops the actuator by preempting a move
Stored-position addresses are bounded by POSITION_ADDRESS_MIN = 0 and POSITION_ADDRESS_MAX = 15
get_actuator_ids returns the actuator id reported by each device for the configured axes
ZaberDevice.homed reads the home-status bit (1 << 7) of each actuator mode
ZaberStage.homed selects the configured axes from the device home status
